nodes.name: Tokens as input
nodes.statement: A transformer reads text as a sequence of tokens. Tokens are words or word pieces drawn from a fixed vocabulary.

nodes.name: Token embeddings
nodes.statement: Each token is mapped to a learned vector of dimension d. A sentence of n tokens becomes an n × d matrix with one row per token.

nodes.name: Dot product as similarity
nodes.statement: The dot product q·k is large when two vectors point in similar directions. So it can score how well a query matches a key.

nodes.name: Queries, keys, values
nodes.statement: Each token vector x is multiplied by three learned matrices. This gives a query q = xW_Q, a key k = xW_K and a value v = xW_V.

nodes.name: Attention scores
nodes.statement: Token i gives every token j the score qᵢ·kⱼ. A high score means token j is relevant to token i.

nodes.name: Softmax weights
nodes.statement: Softmax turns each token's row of scores into positive weights aᵢⱼ that sum to 1.

nodes.name: Softmax saturation
nodes.statement: When scores are very large, softmax puts almost all the weight on a single token. Its gradients then become tiny and learning stalls.

nodes.name: Scaling by √d_k
nodes.statement: For vectors of dimension d_k with independent random entries, the dot product has variance proportional to d_k. Dividing the scores by √d_k keeps them in a range where softmax does not saturate.

nodes.name: Attention as weighted average
nodes.statement: The output for token i is Σⱼ aᵢⱼvⱼ. That is the average of all value vectors, weighted by how much token i attends to each one.

nodes.name: Attention formula
nodes.statement: In matrix form, attention computes softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V for all tokens at once.

nodes.name: No built-in order
nodes.statement: Shuffling the input tokens only shuffles the attention outputs in the same way. So attention by itself ignores word order.

nodes.name: Positional encoding
nodes.statement: Adding a position-dependent vector to each token embedding gives the model the order information that attention lacks.

nodes.name: Multi-head attention
nodes.statement: Multi-head attention runs h attention operations in parallel, each with its own projections of size d/h. Their outputs are concatenated and projected back to size d.

nodes.name: Heads learn different relations
nodes.statement: Because each head has its own projections, different heads can attend by different criteria. One head may track the previous token while another links a pronoun to its noun.

nodes.name: Residual connection
nodes.statement: Each sublayer adds its output to its input, x ← x + F(x). Information and gradients can then pass straight through the whole stack.

nodes.name: Layer normalization
nodes.statement: Layer normalization rescales each token's vector to zero mean and unit variance, followed by a learned scale and shift. This keeps activations in a stable range from layer to layer.

nodes.name: Feed-forward sublayer
nodes.statement: After attention, each token passes separately through the same two-layer network. Its hidden layer is usually about four times wider than d.

nodes.name: Transformer block
nodes.statement: A transformer block is multi-head attention followed by a feed-forward sublayer. Each of the two is wrapped in layer normalization and a residual connection.

nodes.name: Stacking blocks
nodes.statement: A transformer stacks many blocks of the same shape. Later blocks build on relations found by earlier ones, and the residual connections keep deep stacks trainable.

nodes.name: Output projection
nodes.statement: The final vector at each position is multiplied by a d × V matrix, where V is the vocabulary size. Softmax over the result gives a probability for every possible next token.

nodes.name: Next-token objective
nodes.statement: A language model is trained to predict each token from the tokens before it. The loss is the cross-entropy of the predicted distribution against the true next token.

nodes.name: Causal mask
nodes.statement: A decoder sets the scores for all later positions to −∞ before softmax. Token i can then attend only to tokens 1 through i.

nodes.name: No sequential bottleneck
nodes.statement: A recurrent network must process tokens one after another. Attention computes the outputs for all positions at the same time.

nodes.name: Parallel training
nodes.statement: With the causal mask, one forward pass produces a next-token prediction for every position of a sequence. So a whole sequence trains in a single parallel step.

nodes.name: Quadratic cost
nodes.statement: Attention scores every pair of tokens. Its compute and memory therefore grow as n² with the sequence length n.

nodes.name: KV cache
nodes.statement: Under the causal mask, the keys and values of earlier tokens never change during generation. They are stored and reused, so each new token computes only its own query, key and value.

nodes.name: Short path between tokens
nodes.statement: Any two tokens can exchange information in a single attention step. In a recurrent network, the signal must pass through every token between them.
